transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess my mom wanted me to come, mostly. I mean, I know something’s wrong, but it’s hard to explain because it’s not like one big thing happened. It’s more like I just… stopped doing things. I sit in my room most of the time, and I’ll realize I’m wearing the same clothes again, like I just can’t make myself change or shower or even care enough to start.

I used to knit sometimes, and I had a journal, and I’d go for walks when I needed to clear my head, but I don’t really do any of that now. It feels like everything takes this huge amount of effort, even tiny things. My mom asks me what’s wrong and I just kind of sit there, because answering feels like too much too. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it’s like there’s no energy in me to do anything.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I… I don’t know if I’d call it depressed, exactly. Like, I know people say “depressed” and they mean sad or crying all the time, and I’m not sure that’s what it is for me. I don’t really sit there thinking, like, “I’m so sad” every minute. It’s more confusing than that.

Some days I guess I feel low, or kind of flat, but I haven’t been keeping track of whether it’s most of the day or nearly every day. Time kind of blurs together, so when you ask it that specifically, I’m not sure how to answer without guessing. I just know I don’t feel normal, but I don’t know if “down or depressed” is the right word.
Can you think back over the past two weeks — was there a period where most of the time, you felt down, empty, or hopeless for most of the day?

I’m trying to think of the last two weeks like… actual days, but it’s hard because they kind of smear together. I don’t have a clear “yes, from Tuesday to Friday I felt hopeless all day” kind of answer.

I think there were times where I felt empty, maybe. Like not exactly crying or devastated, more like there’s nothing in me and I’m just sitting there. But I don’t know if that was most of the day, or if it was just what I remember because the rest is blank or boring. Hopeless… I don’t know. That word feels really big. I don’t know if I’m hopeless, or if I just can’t picture things changing, which maybe sounds the same but doesn’t feel the same in my head.

So I guess… I’m not sure. I can’t honestly say there was a clear period like that, but I also can’t say I felt okay.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you used to care about?

Yeah… I think that’s probably one of the main things, honestly. I don’t really feel drawn to anything anymore. Like, I used to knit — not constantly or anything, but I’d make little things, or I’d at least have a project sitting there that I cared about. And I used to write in my journal, even if it was just messy thoughts, and sometimes I’d go for walks because it helped me feel like my head was clearer.

Now I just… don’t. The knitting stuff is still there, I can see it, but it’s like it belongs to someone else. I don’t pick it up. I don’t think, “Oh, I want to do that.” I’ll think maybe I should, and then I just sit there anyway. Same with the journal. It feels like too much to even open it, which sounds stupid because it’s just a notebook, but it really does feel like too much.

Mostly I’m just in my room. I’ll be in the same clothes, and I know I should change or shower or do something normal, but I can’t make myself start. It’s not even always that I’m sad about it in the moment. It’s more like there’s no push inside me. My mom will ask what’s wrong or tell me I should go outside, and I barely answer because even explaining it feels like it takes more energy than I have.

So… yeah. I guess I’ve lost interest, or lost the ability to care enough to do those things. It’s like the things I used to enjoy are still technically there, but I can’t reach them.
Can you recall if there was a time when most days, you felt down, low, or empty for the majority of the day, even if it wasn’t every single day?

I’m not sure I can pin that down. Like, when you say “most days” and “majority of the day,” my mind tries to make a calendar out of it, and I don’t really have that. I don’t have a clear memory like, yes, for a whole stretch I woke up empty and stayed that way until night.

I do remember feeling sort of low or empty at different times, but I can’t tell if it was most of the day or if those are just the parts that stand out because everything else felt kind of blank. Some days I’m just sitting there and hours pass, but I don’t know what feeling to call that. It’s not always like I’m actively thinking, “I’m sad.” It’s more like there’s not much there.

So… I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I know I haven’t felt like myself, but I can’t honestly remember a definite period where most days were like that for most of the day.
Over the past few weeks, have you felt a lack of energy or felt tired out, even when you haven’t done anything physically taxing?

Yeah… I think so. It’s hard because I haven’t really been doing anything that should make me tired, so it feels weird to say I’m tired, but I am. Or maybe it’s not even tired like after exercise. It’s more like there’s no energy to start anything.

Mostly I just sit in my room. I’ll still be in the same clothes, and I know I should change or shower or pick up something, anything, but it feels like there’s this big wall before even the smallest thing. Like knitting or writing in my journal or going for a walk used to be normal things, not huge tasks, and now I look at them and just… don’t move. I’ll think, “I should do that,” and then nothing happens.

And when my mom asks what’s wrong, even answering her feels like too much sometimes. I don’t mean to ignore her, but the words feel heavy, like I don’t have enough in me to explain it. So yes, I guess I do feel worn out, but it’s not from doing too much. It’s more like I’m tired before I’ve even done anything.
Looking back at the past two weeks, would you say that on most days, you felt low, empty, or down for most of the day, even if it wasn’t always intense or obvious?

I still don’t know how to answer that exactly. I know you’re asking about the past two weeks specifically, and I’ve been trying to think about it that way, like day by day, but it gets blurry really fast.

I can say I haven’t felt good, or normal. There’s been a lot of just… blankness, I guess. Like I’ll be sitting there and time goes by, and if you asked me in the middle of it, “Are you sad?” I don’t know if I’d say yes. It doesn’t always feel like crying or feeling obviously down. Sometimes it’s more like there’s nothing happening inside, or everything is muted.

But whether that was most days, for most of the day… I don’t feel confident saying yes. I don’t track it well enough. Some parts of days feel empty, and then other parts I’m just kind of existing and not really noticing what I feel. So I don’t want to give you an answer that sounds more certain than I am.

I guess what I can say is that things have felt off and kind of flat, but I can’t clearly say, “Yes, I was low or down most of the day on most days.”
Has there been a time in the past few weeks when you completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, not even feeling a little bit of pleasure or motivation to try them?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if “completely” is the right word, because sometimes I still think, like, I should want to do those things. But I don’t actually do them. It’s like the wanting part doesn’t turn into anything.

I used to knit, or write in my journal, or go for walks, just small things, but they felt like mine, you know? Now I mostly just sit in my room. I’ll be in the same clothes for way too long, and I know that sounds bad, but it’s like even changing feels like this whole task I can’t start. And the knitting stuff is there, and my journal is there, and I can look at it and know I used to care about it, but there’s no pull toward it. I don’t get that little feeling of, “Oh, maybe this will be nice.”

So… yes, I guess in the way you mean, I’ve pretty much lost interest. Not in a dramatic way where I’m upset about each thing, more like everything just sits there and I sit there too. And when my mom asks what’s wrong, even answering her feels like too much effort sometimes. I barely say anything because I don’t have the energy to explain it.
Can you tell me if there was a time when this lack of interest or energy lasted for at least two weeks without much relief?

Yeah… definitely. I mean, if you’re asking whether it was at least two weeks, then yes, much longer than that.

It’s kind of embarrassing to say it out loud because I keep thinking of it as something that maybe started “recently,” but when I actually look back, this whole decline started around when I began the community-college program. That was about two years and two months ago now. It didn’t feel like one clear day where everything changed, but after I started there, things just began slipping, and then they kept slipping.

There might have been little moments where I thought maybe I was going to get back into things, but not really relief in the way you mean. Not like I had a solid stretch where my energy or interest came back and I felt like myself again. It’s more like I’ve been waiting for it to pass, and then months went by, and then it was a year, and now it’s been over two years.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even when you do them?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not even just that I don’t start things, although that’s a big part of it. It’s like even if I try to do something I used to like, there’s no real feeling from it.

Like my knitting stuff is still there, and I’ll see it and remember that I used to get into it, like picking colors or seeing something slowly turn into a scarf or whatever. But now I’ll maybe touch it or think about doing it, and it just feels like… nothing. Or it feels like work before it even starts. Same with my journal. I used to write because it helped me sort things out, but now opening it feels pointless, and if I do write anything it’s just flat.

Mostly I just sit in my room. I stay in the same clothes way too long, and I know I should change or go for a walk or do something normal, but I can’t make myself. And even if I do manage to start, I don’t get that little bit of pleasure or relief from it. It doesn’t feel like, “Oh, I’m glad I did that.” It’s more like I did a task and now I’m tired.

When my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely even answer sometimes, not because I’m trying to be rude, but because explaining it feels like too much effort. I don’t know… it’s like the enjoyment part just doesn’t really show up anymore.

But now I’ll maybe touch it or think about doing it, and it just feels like… nothing. Or it feels like work before it even starts. Same with my journal. I used to write because it helped me sort things out, but now opening it feels pointless, and if I do write anything it’s just flat.

Mostly I just sit in my room. I stay in the same clothes way too long, and I know I should change or go for a walk or do something normal, but I can’t make myself. And even if I do manage to start, I don’t get that little bit of pleasure or relief from it. It doesn’t feel like, “Oh, I’m glad I did that.” It’s more like I did a task and now I’m tired.

When my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely even answer sometimes, not because I’m trying to be rude, but because explaining it feels like too much effort. I don’t know… it’s like the enjoyment part just doesn’t really show up anymore.

inference.note: The patient has experienced a persistent lack of interest, loss of pleasure, low energy, and functional impairment lasting over two years without significant relief. This rules out acute and single-episode depressions (F32.0, F32.1, F32.2, F33.0, F33.1) and supports a diagnosis of Recurrent Depressive Disorder, Current Episode Severe Without Psychotic Symptoms (F33.2).
